name: Tulsa International Airport
before:
Tulsa's airport, five miles north east of downtown, and a working industrial site as much as a passenger terminal. It is the global maintenance headquarters for American Airlines, and Spirit AeroSystems builds Boeing and Gulfstream parts here.

For passengers there are two concourses. Concourse A has eleven gates, seven in use, serving Alaska, Allegiant, American and Delta. Concourse B, rebuilt between 2010 and 2012, has eleven gates with eight in use, for Southwest and United. A 45,000 square foot customs facility allows direct international flights, starting with Mexico.

Three runways cross the 4,360 acre site, the longest at 10,000 feet. The 138th Fighter Wing of the Oklahoma Air National Guard is based alongside.

The aviation industry here dates from the Second World War, when Douglas Aircraft built aircraft at Air Force Plant No. 3 on the south east side. Part of that building now assembles school buses.

The Tulsa Air and Space Museum is on the north west side of the airport. It was called Tulsa Municipal until 1963.
after:
Tulsa's airport, a few miles north east of downtown, and an aerospace industrial site as well as a passenger airport. American Airlines has had a major maintenance base here since 1946.

For passengers there are two concourses. Alaska, Allegiant, American and Delta use Concourse A. Southwest and United use Concourse B, which was renovated between 2010 and 2012. A 45,000 square foot customs facility opened in May 2026, and the first international flights, a seasonal Sun Country service to Cancún, began that month.

Three runways serve the 4,360 acre site, the longest at 10,000 feet. The 138th Fighter Wing of the Oklahoma Air National Guard is based alongside.

During the Second World War, Douglas Aircraft assembled bombers at Air Force Plant 3.

The Tulsa Air and Space Museum is at the airport, which was called Tulsa Municipal until 1963.

claims.inAfter: a few miles north east of downtown
claims.note: Was 'five miles'. Wikipedia's five miles (8 km) fails the coordinates check: the straight line from the GeoNames centre is 10.7 km (6.6 miles), a ratio of 0.76. The FAA record gives 5 nautical miles (about 5.8 statute miles). 'A few miles' is what every source supports. The bearing (63 degrees, north east) passes. OurAirports has no home link for KTUL; flytulsa.com is the site in Wikipedia's infobox and every release on it is issued by the Tulsa Airports Improvement Trust.
